Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: TASK_KILLED is silently lost if the victim blocks before its next reschedule, so kill() is a no-op after resources were already released
FILE: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c
CLAIM: do_kill() defers teardown by setting `victim->status = TASK_KILLED` (line 367) and relies on scheduler()'s `else if (prev->status == TASK_KILLED)` branch (line 66) firing on the victim's hart. But status is a single field that do_block() (line 593) overwrites unconditionally with TASK_BLOCKED. If the flagged victim reaches any blocking call before its next timer tick -- do_sleep(), binsem_op(LOCK), futex_wait(), do_waitpid() -- the TASK_KILLED marker is destroyed. scheduler() then sees prev->status == TASK_BLOCKED, takes neither branch, and the process is left intact in the sleep/block queue with its address space and pcb slot alive; do_unblock() later marks it TASK_READY and it runs forever.

Concrete failure: `exec consensus` then `kill <pid>` of a task currently running on the other hart. consensus.c calls sys_sleep(2) every loop iteration (lines 90, 98, 120), so within the ~10 ms window before the victim's next timer interrupt it almost always enters do_sleep -> do_block. The shell prints "Task(pid=N) killed" but the task keeps running; meanwhile release_resources() already gave away its semaphores, drained its wait_list and cleared its timer node, so it resumes in the inconsistent state described in the previous finding.

/* 
 * trick: during an irq handling, current_running may be modified
 * but $tp will not be modified until ret_from_exception()
 */
ENTRY(enable_preempt)
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  addi t0, t0, -1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  beq t0, zero, do_enable
  jr ra
do_enable:
  not t0, x0
  csrs CSR_SIE, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_preempt)

ENTRY(disable_preempt)
  csrw CSR_SIE, zero  
  ld t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  addi t0, t0, 1
  sd t0, PCB_PREEMPT_COUNT(tp)
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_preempt)

ENTRY(enable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_interrupt)

ENTRY(disable_interrupt)
  li t0, SR_SIE
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_interrupt)

ENTRY(enable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrs CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(enable_sum)

ENTRY(disable_sum)
  li t0, SR_SUM
  csrc CSR_SSTATUS, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(disable_sum)

ENTRY(ret_from_exception)
  ld tp, current_cpu_running
  call unlock_kernel
  RESTORE_CONTEXT

  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, to_user
to_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
  j restore_sp_done
to_user:
  ld sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
restore_sp_done:
  sret
ENDPROC(ret_from_exception)

ENTRY(exception_handler_entry)
  /* use kernel stack to handle exception */
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  bnez tp, from_user

from_kernel:
  csrrw tp, CSR_SSCRATCH, tp
  j store_sp_done
from_user:
  sd sp, PCB_USER_SP(tp)
  ld sp, PCB_KERNEL_SP(tp)
store_sp_done:

  SAVE_CONTEXT
  /* 
   * Disable user-mode memory access as it should only be set in the actual user copy routines.
   * Disable the FPU to detect illegal usage of floating point in kernel space.
   */
  li t0, SR_SUM | SR_FS
  csrc sstatus, t0

  /* load the global pointer */
  .option push
  .option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
  .option pop

  call lock_kernel
  /* 
   * load ret_from_exception into $ra
   * so that we can return to ret_from_exception
   * when interrupt_helper complete.
   */
  la ra, ret_from_exception
  
  /* call interrupt_helper and pass parameters for it */
  mv a0, sp
  csrr a1, CSR_STVAL
  csrr a2, CSR_SCAUSE
  j interrupt_helper
ENDPROC(exception_handler_entry)

ENTRY(clear_ipi)
  li t0, SIE_SSIE
  csrc CSR_SIP, t0
  jr ra
ENDPROC(clear_ipi)

content.text:
I read the actual sources and could not refute this. Everything the claim depends on checks out.

**Verified facts**

- `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c:364-367` — `do_kill()` defers teardown purely by writing `victim->status = TASK_KILLED` when the victim is `TASK_RUNNING` on the other hart, *after* having already called `release_resources(victim)` (line 362, which hands away binsems, drains `wait_list`, and `list_del`s the timer node).
- `sched.c:60-71` — `scheduler()` is the only consumer of that marker (`else if (prev->status == TASK_KILLED)`).
- `sched.c:593-598` — `do_block()` writes `status = TASK_BLOCKED` unconditionally; there is no read-modify-check.
- `status` is the only channel: `grep -rn TASK_KILLED` over the whole tree yields exactly `sched.h:61`, `sched.c:{66,320,350,364,367}`. `pcb_t` (`include/os/sched.h:75-126`) has no separate kill flag.
- No wake-up of the peer hart: `sbi_send_ipi` appears only once, in `kernel/sched/smp.c:27` (boot). So the marker can only be consumed by the victim hart's *own* next `scheduler()` call, which happens either from `reset_irq_timer()` (`kernel/irq/irq.c`, every `timer_interval = time_base/100` ≈ 10 ms) or from a blocking path — and every blocking path calls `do_block()` first.
- Clobbering call sites reachable before that tick: `do_sleep` (`sched.c:332`), `do_waitpid` (`sched.c:417` — this one is *new* code itself), `kernel/locking/binsem.c:39`, `kernel/locking/futex.c:55`, `kernel/syscall/mailbox.c:63,85`.
- The global kernel lock (`entry.S`: `call lock_kernel` in `exception_handler_entry`, `call unlock_kernel` in `ret_from_exception`) does not help — it only guarantees the victim is in user mode (or spinning at `lock_kernel`) while `do_kill` runs; the moment hart 0 releases it, hart 1 proceeds into `do_sleep`/`futex_wait` and overwrites the flag.
- Reachability of the scenario: `test/test_shell.c:345` calls `sys_kill(pid)` and prints "Task(pid=N) killed" on return 1; `do_exec` (`sched.c:236`) inherits the shell's `mask` (`init/main.c`: `pcb[0].mask = 3`), so children are runnable on hart 1; `test/consensus.c:90,98,120` call `sys_sleep(2)` and every loop iteration also runs `mthread_barrier_wait` → `sys_binsem_op(LOCK)` / `sys_futex_wait` (`tiny_libc/mthread.c:13-25`), both of which reach `do_block`.

**Why the window is real, not theoretical**: conditional on `do_kill` catching the victim in `TASK_RUNNING`, the victim is by construction inside the short non-blocking stretch of its loop (a `printf` plus a barrier), so it reaches a `do_block` far sooner than the ≤10 ms until its next timer tick. After that, `scheduler()` at `sched.c:60` takes neither branch, the pcb sits in `sleep_queue`/`block_queue` with its `pgdir` intact, and the later `do_unblock` (`sched.c:601`) puts it back on the ready queue — while its semaphores were already given to an heir (`release_binsem`, `sched.c:260-274`) and its waiters already woken.

The only nuance I'd add to the reviewer's write-up is that hitting a `TASK_RUNNING` victim is itself ~1/N likely for N consensus tasks (they spend most wall-clock time asleep, i.e. `TASK_BLOCKED`, where `do_kill` correctly takes the immediate-teardown `else` branch). That affects reproduction frequency, not correctness — and the deferred path is the entire reason the `TASK_KILLED` state exists in the new code.
